adj_same_paper_reason: Different articles: Paper A (Bulman et al., 2021) is titled 'Genomic Features Associated with the Degree of Phenotypic Resistance to Carbapenems in CR-Kp' and studies carbapenem MIC correlates; Paper B (JAC 2022) is 'Aminoglycoside-resistance gene signatures are predictive of aminoglycoside MICs for CR-Kp' — a different research question (aminoglycosides), different journal/year. Likely the same Northwestern CR-Kp collection and group, but two distinct publications, not a preprint/published pair.
adj_justification_quote: We performed genomic characterization of 166 clinical K. pneumoniae isolates to evaluate genetic correlates with levels of carbapenem resistance. ... Sequencing reads and assembled genomes have been submitted to GenBank under BioProject PRJNA395086.
adj_reasoning: ENA PRJNA395086 is K. pneumoniae genome sequencing with 166 taxon samples. Paper A describes generating and depositing exactly these genomes: it sequenced 166 clinical CR-Kp isolates and states the reads/assemblies were submitted under BioProject PRJNA395086 — the deposit statement marks it as the primary study. The sample count (166) matches the ENA metadata exactly. Paper B addresses aminoglycoside resistance in CR-Kp and (with no text provided) appears to be a companion study reusing the same Northwestern isolate collection rather than the depositing study. Treating Paper A as the found candidate, it is the correct primary study for this project.
adj_rule_gap: When multiple papers from the same lab use the same isolate collection, a finder can be misled into accepting a companion paper that merely reuses the genomes; distinguishing the depositing paper requires anchoring on the explicit 'submitted under BioProject <accession>' data-availability statement plus exact sample-count match, not just topical/cohort overlap.

chosen_title: Pervasive transmission of a carbapenem resistance plasmid in the gut microbiota of hospitalized patients.
paper_title: The distribution of fitness effects of plasmid pOXA-48 in clinical enterobacteria
adj_same_paper_reason: Different works. Paper A (Leon-Sampedro et al., PMC7610705) is the R-GNOSIS transmission study that sequenced the 250-isolate pOXA-48 collection. Paper B (PMC10433420) is a separate CRISPR-Cas9 curing/fitness-effects study with its own primary deposit (PRJNA962867) that explicitly cites Paper A as reference [1] ('The remaining R-GNOSIS sequences can be found in Leon-Sampedro et al. [1]'). Different titles, authors, methods, and cohort framing (250 transmission isolates vs a 35/60-strain curing subset); not a preprint/published pair.
adj_justification_quote: In total, we determined the sequences of 250 isolates by short read methods and two of these genomes and six pOXA-48 plasmids were also sequenced by long-read methods to allow hybrid assembly
adj_reasoning: ENA PRJNA626430 describes 'Whole genome sequence information from 250 enterobacteria clones to characterise the dissemination routes of the carbapenemase-encoding plasmid pOXA-48 in a hospital setting over a period of two years.' Paper A matches this exactly: it generated and deposited the 250-isolate R-GNOSIS pOXA-48 collection (Illumina HiSeq4000 + PacBio, GenBank MT441554/MT989343-49) over the March 2014-March 2016 period, and is the primary study describing the project. Paper B is downstream reuse: its main data live under PRJNA962867, it deposited only six long-read closed wild-type genomes into the pre-existing PRJNA626430, and it directs readers to Leon-Sampedro et al. (=Paper A) for 'the remaining R-GNOSIS sequences.' Thus Paper A describes this project and Paper B merely reuses/cites the data.
adj_rule_gap: A finder keying on accession mentions can be fooled: a secondary reuse paper (Paper B) explicitly names PRJNA626430 and even deposited a few closed genomes into it, yet it cites the primary study for the bulk of the data. Mention of an accession + a handful of deposited records does not equal being the originating study.

chosen_title: Nested Russian Doll-Like Genetic Mobility Drives Rapid Dissemination of the Carbapenem Resistance Gene blaKPC.

Paper A is 'Nested Russian Doll-Like Genetic Mobility Drives Rapid Dissemination of blaKPC' (PMC4879409), a multispecies (13-species) Enterobacteriaceae blaKPC outbreak study of 281 isolates. Paper B carries a distinct title ('KPC-Producing K. pneumoniae at a Single Institution: Insights into Endemicity from WGS'), and the body text actually provided for it is an unrelated biochemistry abstract on glutamate dehydrogenase enzyme kinetics — no shared title, authors, cohort, or findings.
adj_justification_quote: Sequence data obtained in this study have been deposited at the National Center for Biotechnology Information under BioProject no. PRJNA246471.
adj_reasoning: Paper A explicitly names the deposition BioProject PRJNA246471 — exactly THIS project accession — and is the primary study that generated and deposited the genomes: prospective UVA collection, Illumina sequencing of all isolates, PacBio long-read sequencing, and analysis of 281 Enterobacteriaceae isolates. This matches the ENA project ('Genome sequencing of KPC-producing Gammaproteobacteria', multispecies blaKPC plasmid tracking). Paper B's supplied text is an unrelated glutamate dehydrogenase abstract that mentions nothing about KPC, this cohort, or PRJNA246471, so it cannot be shown to describe or even reuse this project from the evidence given. Thus Paper A (the found paper) is the one that describes the project; Paper B does not.
adj_rule_gap: Curated/finder entry pairs a paper title with a completely mismatched abstract body (glutamate dehydrogenase text under a KPC title), which defeats content-based verification — the pipeline should detect title/body topic incoherence and flag the metadata as corrupt rather than trusting the attached text.

adj_same_paper_reason: Paper A is a primary single-hospital genomic outbreak investigation (QECH, Malawi neonatal unit; 86 K. pneumoniae genomes; STs 340/14/372) that explicitly deposited its genomes under PRJEB19322. Paper B is a multi-region meta-analysis of genome-predicted capsule/O serotype prevalence and vaccine coverage across Africa and South Asia, hosted on Pathogenwatch/medRxiv. Different titles, scope (single outbreak vs aggregated meta-analysis), aims and findings — not the same work nor a preprint/published pair.
adj_justification_quote: The Klebsiella pneumoniae genome sequences completed using an Illumina platform from this study are deposited in GenBank under project no. PRJNA641987 ... and the European Nucleotide Archive under project no. PRJEB19322
adj_reasoning: PRJEB19322 is a Sanger pre-publication ESKAPE-pathogen deposit from a single Malawian hospital (QECH). Paper A is the primary study that generated and deposited the K. pneumoniae subset of these genomes — it names PRJEB19322 in both its Data Summary and methods ('subjected to whole genome sequencing ... at the Wellcome Sanger Centre ... deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive ... under project number PRJEB19322'), and the cohort (QECH neonatal/paediatric K. pneumoniae BSIs, 2012–2015) matches the project description. Paper B is a downstream meta-analysis that aggregates/reuses many published Klebsiella datasets for serotype-prevalence and vaccine-coverage estimation; no text and no indication it generated or deposited PRJEB19322 genomes. Thus Paper A (the found candidate) describes this project; Paper B does not.
adj_rule_gap: PRJEB19322 is a broad multi-species 'Sequencing_ESKAPE_pathogens' umbrella deposit (92 samples spanning Enterococcus, S. aureus, K. pneumoniae, Acinetobacter, Pseudomonas, Enterobacter). A single primary paper (here, the K. pneumoniae one) may cover only one species subset, so such umbrella Sanger pre-publication projects can have several legitimate primary papers; the finder should not assume one species-specific paper accounts for the whole accession.
